subject: Co-sell eligibility audit + product page items
messages:

Subject: Co-sell eligibility - quick audit + product page items

Hi Neha / Kimberly,

Thanks again for jumping on the partner intake last week. AWS co-sell team is prepping an eligibility audit for DataForge's upcoming listing and asked for a short checklist and the product page copy we plan to publish. Goal: capture any claim language that needs legal sign-off and confirm we have the required assets (AMI tags, screenshots, SKU mapping). Deadline for the co-sell intake is EOD 2026-02-28 to make the next intake batch.

Can you share: 1) final headline and 3 bullets for the offer page, 2) an AMI image named in the merchant account, 3) the primary SKU and whether we'll support private offers for trials?

I attached the AWS co-sell requirements doc that lists the claim do's and don'ts and the minimum asset set. Happy to jump on a 20-min call if helpful.

Attachments: aws_co-sell_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Elena Park
Partner Solutions Manager — AWS GTM
Amazon Web Services
elena.park@aws-partner.com

Elena — thanks for the checklist, forwarding our working answers below.

On Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 09:12 AM Elena Park <elena.park@aws-partner.com> wrote:
> Hi Neha / Kimberly,
> 
> Thanks again for jumping on the partner intake last week....

Quick responses and action owners:
- Headline + bullets (copy): Kimberly will finalize wording and attach the page draft by COB Monday (action: kimberly_park).
- AMI image + seller/AMI mapping: Ben will confirm seller ID and provide the AMI filename we intend to use (action: ben_carter).
- Private offers/trials: We plan to enable Private Offers for qualified accounts; Tessa will own the trial terms and pricing notes (action: tessa_morgan).
- Legal claims: We noted a claim about "99.9% inference uptime" in the draft; can Legal sign off or should we reword to "designed for high availability"? If Legal needs to see, we'll route via Product Legal and flag here.

Inline draft headline (work-in-progress):
"High-throughput LLM serving engineered for predictable latency and cost"
Bullets (3):
• Production-grade runtime with GPU-aware batching and KV cache optimizations
• Deployment across hosted, dedicated, and private environments for compliance needs
• Cost controls: intelligent batching, quantization suggestions, and token-level telemetry

CTA suggestion: "Start a free trial — contact us for a Private Offer"

Attachments we'll upload to the Seller Console: productpage_draft_v2.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), ami_hero_1.png (image/png) — Ben will share the final AMI name by EOD Monday.

If that timeline works I'll mark us as ready for intake.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Partner GTM — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinfer.com

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinfer.com <kimberly.park@redwoodinfer.com>

Neha / team / Elena — attaching a cleaned-up page draft with simplified claims and alternate CTAs. I toned down the uptime line and added a short "How it works" explainer to satisfy typical AWS review questions.

Key edits:
- Headline tightened: "Predictable LLM inference — low latency, lower cost"
- Claim removed: "99.9% inference uptime" replaced with: "Engineered to meet strict latency SLOs for production workloads"
- Added two short concrete examples under bullets that show cost/latency improvements for typical workloads.
- CTA variants: "Request a Private Offer" and a secondary "Start a hosted trial" for PLG flow.

Attachment: productpage_draft_v2.docx (updated)

If AWS legal asks for an availability SLA figure, we should propose a monitored SLA only for Dedicated customers — otherwise keep public-facing copy qualitative.

- Kimberly
Product Marketing Manager — Redwood Inference
